steps.title: Rinse and Plate Snails
steps.instruction: Rinse patent Biomphalaria glabrata snails (at least 5 weeks post infection with a single miracidium) individually with MilliQ water using wide-tip featherweight forceps to prevent cross-contamination.

substeps.instruction: Place rinsed snails into individual wells of 6- or 12-well plates.
Add 3-4ml of MilliQ water to each well.

steps.title: Induce Cercariae Shedding
steps.instruction: Place snails under direct light for up to 2 hours or until cercariae are visible to the naked eye.

substeps.instruction: Remove snails not shedding cercariae after 2 hours and place in a new tank with food for re-shedding in one week (dispose of if still not shedding by 8 weeks post exposure).
Remove snails shedding low amounts (<100 cercariae) and place in a new tank with food for re-shedding in one week.
Mark wells of shedding snails with an 'X' and assign a unique number to each snail to be preserved throughout the process.

steps.title: Collect Cercariae
steps.instruction: Collect cercariae from each snail into numbered 5ml Eppendorf tubes fitted with a 100µm pluriStrainer Mini.

substeps.instruction: Using a new sterile transfer pipet for each snail, pipette water containing cercariae through the pluriStrainer.
Rinse the well and snails with fresh MilliQ water and collect this water to fill each 5ml tube to the top.
Discard pluriStrainers, close tubes, and submerge in ice for 30 minutes.
Centrifuge tubes at 2000 rpm, 4 °C, for 30 minutes.
Immediately place tubes back on ice and aspirate/pipette off liquid, leaving no more than 50µl of water on the cercariae pellet.

steps.title: Perform Alkaline Lysis
steps.instruction: Lyse the cercariae using 2x Alkaline Lysis Reagent (composed of 25ml H2O, 125µl 10N NaOH, and 20µl 0.5M disodium EDTA; make fresh every 1-2 months, store at RT).

substeps.instruction: Add 1x volume of 2x Alkaline Lysis Reagent to each pellet (e.g., 25µl reagent to 25µl cercariae in MilliQ) and mix well.
Incubate at 95 °C for ~1 hour or until cercariae dissolve, mixing at least every 15 min (centrifuge with mini-centrifuge if needed).
Place on ice to cool.

steps.title: Neutralize Lysate
steps.instruction: Neutralize the lysate using 2x Neutralizing Reagent (composed of 23ml H2O and 2ml 1M Tris-HCl [6.057g Tris-HCl to 50ml nuclease-free H2O]; store at RT).

substeps.instruction: Add 1x volume of 2x Neutralizing Reagent to the lysate (e.g., 50µl reagent to 50µl lysate) and briefly vortex to mix.

steps.title: Prepare PCR Master Mixes
steps.instruction: Prepare two PCR master mixes on ice for actin control and W1 primer sets. Include samples, 1 female positive control, 1 male negative control, and 1 water blank control.

substeps.instruction: Use W1 primers: W1a (5’ CAA CAC AGT GAA ATT CTT CC 3’) and W1b (5’ GAA TTC ACC ACT CGA CAT TC 3’).
Use actin primers: SmAct-F (5’ CAG TGT TCC CTT CCA TCG TT 3’) and SmAct-R (5’ GGA CAG GGT GTT CTT CTG GA 3’).

Assemble 10µl reactions: 6.32µl Nuclease-free water, 0.08µl Platinum II Taq (0.04U/µl), 2µl 5x Platinum II Buffer, 0.2µl 10mM dNTP (0.2mM each), 0.2µl 10uM F primer (0.2uM), 0.2µl 10uM R primer (0.2uM), and 1µl DNA (adjust volume if Nanodrop measurement suggests, but keep DNA <10% of total volume).

steps.title: Amplify and Analyze DNA
steps.instruction: Run the PCR program and analyze the results via gel electrophoresis.

substeps.instruction: PCR Program: Initial denaturation 94°C (2 min); Denature 98°C (5 sec x 25); Anneal and extend 60°C (15 sec); Hold 4°C.
Run a 1% agarose gel to analyze 5-10µl of PCR product.
Interpret results: Males show actin band only; Females show both actin and W1 bands.
